summary: Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani (1917–2001) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Samaldas Arts College, Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, and under Muni Jinvijaya, later holding posts at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, Gujarat University, and the Lalbhai Dalpatbhai Institute of Indology.

Harjot Oberoi is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at St. Stephen's College, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the Australian National University before taking up a chair in Punjabi and Sikh Studies at the University of British Columbia around 1987.

Harogadde Manappa Nayak (1931–2000) was an Indian scholar in linguistics and Indology. He served as Director at the University of Mysore (~1967–1991) and as Vice-chancellor of Gulbarga University (1984–1987).

Harold G. Coward (born 1936) specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. After earning a doctoral degree in philosophy from McMaster University (~1970–1973), he held posts as a professor at the University of Calgary (~1974–1992) and director at the University of Victoria (~1992–2004).

Harold Hargreaves (1876–1951) was an Indologist and archaeologist. After serving as headmaster at Government Senior Secondary School, Amritsar (~1908–1914), he held multiple posts in the Archaeological Survey of India, including Superintendent and Deputy Director General (1928–1931).

Harold Scheub (1931–2019) studied at the University of Michigan, UCLA, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, earning his PhD there (~1965–1969). He taught at Valparaiso University (~1960–1964) before serving as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–2013).
Harold Stewart (1916–1995) worked in the fields of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his studies at the University of Sydney and the Sydney Conservatorium of Music.

Harold Walter Bailey (1899–1996) was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological linguistics. He studied at the University of Western Australia and Oxford under Frederick William Thomas, later holding posts at SOAS and the Sanskrit chair at Cambridge (1936–1967).

Haroon Khan Sherwani (1891–1980) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Aligarh Muslim University, Oxford, and under Ghulam Yazdani, and later served on faculties at Osmania University (~1919–1948), Nizam College, and Zakir Husain Delhi College.

Harry Falk (born 1947) is a scholar of Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Gaya Charan Tripathi and served as Director at the Free University of Berlin from 1993 to 2012.
Hartmut Buescher is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Chandrabhal Tripathi. He has held posts at the University of Copenhagen and the Royal Danish Library.
Hartmut Scharfe (1932–2020) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He completed his doctoral studies under Paul Thieme and later held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles.

Hartmut-Ortwin Feistel is an Indology scholar who held positions as director at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 1989), the Prussian State Library (attested 1982–1994), and the Verzeichnis der Orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland (attested 1992–1993).

Haruhiko Masaki (born 1938) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. After studying at Gakushuin University and completing master's and doctoral courses at the University of Tokyo (~1961–1967), he served as a professor at Nagasaki University (attested 1988).
Haruka Yanagisawa (1944–2015) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (~1993–2007) and Chiba University (attested 2005).

Harumi Hirano Ziegler specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed her MA and PhD degrees at the University of California, Los Angeles, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Robert Buswell.

Harunaga Isaacson (born 1965) is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Groningen and Leiden, notably under Hans T. Bakker and Tilmann Vetter, and held academic posts at Oxford, Groningen, Penn, and Hamburg.

Harushige Kōzu (1908–1973) was a linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Oxford's Balliol College under Naoshiro Tsuji. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1938–1948) and Musashi University (from 1968).

Harvey B. Aronson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Richard Hugh Robinson among others, and he held posts at the University of Virginia (attested 1988) and as co-director of the Dawn Mountain Center for Tibetan Buddhism.

Haya Akegarasu (1877–1954) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure. He studied under Manshi Kiyozawa and at Otani University and Tokyo School of Foreign Languages, later serving as head of administration at Higashi Hongan-ji (~1951–1954).
